verdicts.quote: A clean file creates every user atomically; any problem creates none
then a table of row, column, problem (and "duplicates row N" for `duplicate_in_file`); when truncated, a line `and {T-100} more`.
A later row with the same email is `duplicate_in_file` and reports `related_row` (the owner's row number). A row whose email matches any existing user of any status is `already_exists`.
An admin may assign either role through import, the same authority as single-user creation. … If single creation restricts it, import must match
the import screen and the import operation are available only to a signed-in user whose *current* role is admin.
verdicts.missing: The admin-role check is explicit. The spec does not say whether import permission can be withheld from an admin who may create users individually.

verdicts.quote: the first record is the header. … `email` and `name` must be present; `role` may be absent. … `missing_column` (lists the missing canonical names), then `unknown_column` (lists 1-based column positions, never the cell text)
UTF-8 with an optional BOM, comma delimiter, line ends LF or CRLF … FX-4 creates names `Hopper, Grace` … `invalid_characters` … including tab or a line break from a quoted field
A rejected import (FX-5) sends no onboarding message and issues no token. … if sending is not atomic with the commit, the compensation rule is a G-1 decision before this line is final.
verdicts.missing: The builder still needs a rule for an invitation already sent before a later row fails, or a dispatch rule that prevents this sequence.

verdicts.quote: exactly 5,000 data rows is accepted; 5,001 is rejected. … `too_many_rows`, 422, nothing created, no row validation performed.
a 0-byte or BOM-only file is empty … `no_data_rows`, `too_many_rows` (R-2, R-3, R-4) … `created_count` equals the number of data rows: 1 for FX-16
Admin A submits FX-1 twice from S0: first 201 (7 users); second 422 with `already_exists` on rows 2, 3 and 4, `row_error_total` 3; still 7 users.
Processing is synchronous within one request; the result is the response. … `{N} users created` (`1 user created` when N is 1) and a link to the user list
verdicts.missing: Even the largest accepted file runs synchronously. Background processing would need a way for the admin to receive or retrieve the result after the upload request ends.

verdicts.quote: Importing the 5,000 users of FX-17a sends 5,000 onboarding messages and not more or fewer, **if** single creation sends one
verdicts.missing: The builder still has to decide whether those messages go out together or in batches, and at what rate.

verdicts.quote: the initial status, onboarding (for example an invitation or set-password message) and any per-user audit event match what the product does for one user created by an admin. No password is read from the file.
verdicts.missing: The referenced single-user flow is unknown. The initial account status, whether a password exists at creation, and the first sign-in steps remain unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Uploaded bytes | the request handler's memory (A-10) | nobody else | n/a: request-scoped | request end, success or failure

actor id (absent when unauthenticated), timestamp, outcome (`created`, `rejected`, `forbidden`, `error`), file size in bytes when read, data-row count when parsed, `created_count`, the file-level code or the row-error total.
a fixed file can be re-uploaded whole. … submit and file controls disabled, an indeterminate busy indication
verdicts.missing: The spec gives a whole-file retry. It does not define cancellation after submission or an action to retry only failed rows.

verdicts.quote: an indeterminate busy indication and the text "Creating users…" … **Numeric time bound: unresolved**, because the platform and its limit are not known
verdicts.missing: The busy indicator is specified. A maximum completion time for the largest accepted file is still open.

verdicts.quote: an existing behaviour must be preserved once found (single-user creation, authorization) … An email that already exists, or repeats within the file, is an error. No update, skip or merge.

neutralising spreadsheet-formula prefixes on later export (not stored differently; any future export owns that). … FX-23 (a 2,000,000-character name inside the size limit): 422 with one row error `too_long` on row 2 name
